mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.0%, it signals a monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a favorable monetary policy environment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL is falling (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as stronger housing activity signals robust economic growth and increased corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds 2200 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls below 2000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising housing starts (HOUST) and falling industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is rising and INDPRO is falling (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.2% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL rising > 0.3% in 3 months), the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
